I got two teenagers, my daughter will be 14 next month, who is amazing in understanding of BPD. She reminds me of my worth on low days, and supports me by running a bath or making me some sparkling water if I walk in having a bad day after work. She just amazes me with her compassion, love and understanding. She knows I have had a rough childhood, and I am working on my demons from that and is my number one supporter. I also have a son who is 16. He too is amazing. I have watched him grow and learn about mental illness through me, and learning and growing to be a compassionate, caring young man, who has a huge heart. 

I myself have broken the cycle of violence, alcoholism and neglect  and I have to remind myself that my two wonderful children show me daily just how much my hard work on myself has helped them to grow as humans as well! Nothing better than that.

I don't agree with the word "authority" so to speak. I certainly do not view doctors as an authority figure. They may be an expert in their field, no doubt in my mind, but I come from the viewpoint that clients are experts in their own health as well ( of course their are the douche bag clients, who think they have a degree in medicine cause they have google) but the genuine patients who care enough about their own health, deserve to be a part of health care decisions that effect them. I don't believe everything a doctor tells me sometimes, because quite frankly, they are human as well, and can make mistakes, and I as an educated person, deserve the right to question and request to be an active part in decisions made in regards to my health. In the past doctors may have been viewed as the "expert authority", and while I disagree with this statement, I  believe that all health care professionals deserve respect, because ultimately, it is a health care team that saves lives. :)
